newsitem.title: USA: Brady bonds mixed, most follow Treasuries lower.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds mixed, most follow Treasuries lower.

text.p: Emerging markets debt traded mixed on Tuesday as Treasuries' losses pulled most Bradys lower, traders said.
Spreads over Treasuries were wider for most countries, suffering from a lack of buyer interest after the Memorial Day holiday, traders said.
"It's been pretty quiet the last three days," said a trader at a U.S. investment bank. "Customer flows are on the lighter side, although I think most people are still on the defensive right now."

Late on Tuesday, benchmark Brazil "C" bonds had given back some of their recent gains to stand off 3/4 at 78-7/8 bid. Argentina Pars were off 1/2 at 66-5/8 bid, and Mexico Pars had dipped 5/8 to 74-1/4 bid.
"I think we're just in a consolidation phase," another trader said. "We're still pretty close to all-time tight spreads," he added.
Ecuador Brady bonds offered the day's best performance, with PDIs up 7/8 at 63-1/2 bid and Discounts up 5/8 at 69-1/8.
"Ecuador traded a little higher on the referendum news," one trader said.

Preliminary returns from Sunday's plebiscite showed between 62 and 65 percent of Ecuador voters endorsed interim president Fabian Alarcon and 74 percent supported the February ouster of President Abdala Bucaram.

U.S.-based analysts said the poll soothed fears about Ecuador's near-term political scenario, but they said Alarcon still did not have the popular support required to implement harsh austerity measures.
Among losing issues, Venezuela and Panama paper tallied some of the greatest losses. Traded volume was thin for both countries' debt, however, traders said.
Venezuela Pars were off 7/8 at 75-3/8 bid, and Panama Pars were down 1-1/4 at 58 bid.
"Pars tend to outperform on up Treasuries days and underperform on down Treasuries days," one trader said.
Elsewhere, Bulgaria IABs were off 1/8 at 67-5/8 bid, dollar-denominated Russian Vnesh loans were off 1/8 at 85-7/8 and Phillippines Pars were down 3/8 at 86-3/4.
The bellwether 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was off 15/32 to yield 7.03 percent.
